name: Tlacolulita Zapotec
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: En las lenguas transyautepequeñas el contraste fortis/lenis se neutraliza en palabras no prominentes de la frase. (16) Tlacolulita kʲaʰt 'tortilla' ˌkʲaðeˈnaʔk 'tortilla de ayer' [p.21] ... La neutralización del contraste fortis/lenis en la raíz no prominente de una frase nominal/palabra compuesta parece ser una innovación transyautepequeña. Podemos imaginar que existe en Tlacolulita tanto como en Petapa [COLOV VIII slide 38]
new_statements.translation: In the Transyautepecan languages the fortis/lenis contrast is neutralized in non-prominent words of the phrase. (16) Tlacolulita kʲaʰt 'tortilla', ˌkʲaðeˈnaʔk 'yesterday's tortilla' ... The neutralization of the fortis/lenis contrast in the non-prominent root of a noun phrase/compound word appears to be a Transyautepecan innovation. We can imagine that it exists in Tlacolulita as well as in Petapa.
new_statements.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2018. "Diversificación y convergencia: una reconsideración del 'zapoteco de la Sierra Sur' y la filiación del cisyautepequeño". Paper presented at the Seminario de Diacronía y sincronía en lenguas tipológicamente diversas, Universidad de Sonora, 12-13 Nov 2018 (author-posted PDF); supplemented by Beam de Azcona 2018, "El zapoteco de Tlacolulita y el transyautepequeño, el legado lingüístico de Cosijoeza I", slides, COLOV VIII, Oaxaca.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No published rule for word-level stress placement. What the principal documenter's work shows: the language is tonal (contrastive tones, low tone with breathy voice, e.g. /jòʃ/ [jo̤ʃ˨˩] 'avocado'); in her transcriptions stress is marked on the (usually monosyllabic) root and never on TAM prefixes (PFV /biˈɾe/, POT /iˈɾe/ 'run out'; /biˈtʃɛ̀ʔ/ 'filled up'; mbi-ˈsi 'eagle', mbiˈɡupe 'armadillo'), i.e. the pan-Zapotec root-initial ('trochaic') stress that she reconstructs for Proto Trochaic Zapotec; in noun phrases/compounds the final (modifier) root carries primary prominence and the first root is non-prominent, with fortis/lenis neutralized there (kʲaʰt 'tortilla' but ˌkʲaðeˈnaʔk 'yesterday's tortilla', ˌkʲaðenaˈlasˑ 'thin tortilla').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; the transcriptions mark the non-prominent first root of a compound/NP with a secondary-stress sign (ˌkʲaðeˈnaʔk).
new_statements.domain_note: The explicit statement concerns phrase/compound-level prominence, not the location of stress within a word; word-level placement is only inferable from stress-marked transcriptions of elicited forms (prefix + monosyllabic root). Citation forms elicited by the author with speaker Roque Julián de la Rosa (fieldwork 2016-2018).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog tlac1240 = ISO zpk, the Zapotec of Asunción Tlacolulita (Yautepec district, Oaxaca; a Zapotec island in Chontal territory), autonym tì'ch nò (Beam de Azcona) / tixh nguizë (INALI 2008). Glottolog/Ethnologue/Wikipedia file it under Southern Zapotec (Smith Stark 2007; Beam de Azcona 2014 grouped it with Amatec/Macro-Coatecan), but Beam de Azcona 2018 onward reclassifies it as Transyautepecan, a Central Zapotec subgroup, alongside the Petapa-Guevea dialect chain. Glottolog's sole 'descriptive' reference, Rendón 1970 'Notas fonológicas del zapoteco de Tlacochahuaya', is a name-collision error: it describes San Jerónimo Tlacochahuaya (Tlacolula Valley Zapotec, ISO zab), not Tlacolulita. All first-hand Tlacolulita data examined come from Beam de Azcona's own fieldwork (2016-2018, speaker Roque Julián de la Rosa).

sources.note: p.21 §4: 'En las lenguas transyautepequeñas el contraste fortis/lenis se neutraliza en palabras no prominentes de la frase. (16) Tlacolulita kʲaʰt tortilla / ˌkʲaðeˈnaʔk tortilla de ayer' — phrase-level prominence on the final root, first root non-prominent (secondary mark). p.5 general: Chatino has root-final stress, Zapotec root-initial. No explicit Tlacolulita word-stress rule.

sources.note: Slides on 'La hipótesis del acento sensible al peso prosódico' concern Proto-Zapotecan/Soltec/Petapa, not Tlacolulita. Slide 'La realización fonético del tono bajo': 'Algunas lenguas zapotecas (Lachixío, Tlacolulita, entre otros) suelen tener voz murmurada fonéticamente en sílabas con tono bajo. Tlacolulita aguacate /jòʃ/ [jo̤ʃ˨˩]' (language is tonal). Slide 51 cites Beam de Azcona, en preparación, 'Zapotecan Stress and its Interaction with Phonological Contrasts: Evidence from Collaborative Linguistics and...'.
